name: Ochraceous-Salmon
lede: Ochraceous-Salmon is a light, ochre-tinted orange whose compound name Robert Ridgway coined in 1912 for the color guide he built for naturalists.

sections.title: An ochre-toned salmon
sections.body:
The name joins *ochraceous*, meaning ochre-colored, to *salmon*, the pink-orange of the fish's flesh, a compound in the style Robert Ridgway used throughout his 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* [1]. The ISCC-NBS committee later filed the same Ridgway name into its own 1955 dictionary, in block 53 [2].

The identical hex also happens to be the closest match on file to *Sharegaki* (洒落柿, "stylish persimmon"), a Japanese traditional color; the resemblance is a coincidence of measurement, not a shared origin, since Ridgway's English compound and the Japanese name were coined independently [1][3]. The nearest English look-alikes are [[sandy-brown]], [[apricot]] and [[apricot-buff|Apricot Buff]], all close to the same shade [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A close match appears in 59 of our 23,781 archived paintings, about 0.25 per cent, with the within-painting lens finding it in 35, rarer than 55 per cent of our named colors [4]. It peaks in the 1500s, 1.5 times the archive's overall rate for that century (6 paintings), and most often plays an accent rather than a shadow or highlight [4]. The earliest dated match is Masaccio's work from 1423, 489 years before Ridgway's 1912 name; that gap is a floor, not a first sighting, since the match is a look-alike color in an aged, varnished photograph, as photographed, not a pigment test [4].

issues: No concordance hits (src empty); written from ColorHub graph/library data (Ridgway 1912, ISCC-NBS 1955).

Fixed: the name section cited a specific Ridgway plate/hue ('plate XV at hue 13 prime, tone b') that does not match any node in data/graph/nodes-o.json or any other source file in this repo (the only Ridgway plate XV entry on file is for the unrelated ochraceous-orange, at hue 15', not 13'). Removed the unsupported plate/hue detail; kept only the ISCC-NBS block 53 attribution to Ridgway, which data/sources/iscc-nbs-names.json does support.
